ai.text:
The Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act requires the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to gather information from federal agencies and report to Congress on federally funded projects that are running late or costing much more than originally expected.

Under the act, OMB must issue guidance telling federal agencies to send it information each year about two kinds of projects: those that are more than five years behind schedule, and those whose spending is at least $1 billion more than the original cost estimate.

For each of these projects, agencies must report several things. These include a description of the project, an explanation of any change to its original scope, and the original and current expected completion dates. They must also give the original and current cost estimates, both adjusted for inflation, along with an explanation of any delays or cost increases. Finally, they must report any award, incentive fee, or other bonus given for the project, along with the amount and the reason for it.

OMB must then compile this information into an annual report for Congress and post the report on its website.
